results.title: Epistemic models
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Given a type of worlds $W$, a type of atoms and a type of agents, an epistemic model consists of a binary accessibility relation $R_i$ on $W$ for each agent $i$ and a valuation assigning to each world the atoms true there; the world type $W$ is required to be nonempty.

results.title: Epistemic formulas
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Given a type of atoms and a type of agents, the formulas of epistemic logic are built inductively: every atom $p$ is a formula, falsity $\bot$ is a formula, if $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are formulas then so is the implication $\varphi \to \psi$, and if $\varphi$ is a formula and $i$ is an agent then $K_i \varphi$ (read "agent $i$ knows $\varphi$") is a formula.

results.title: Negation of epistemic formulas
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The negation $\neg\varphi$ of an epistemic formula $\varphi$ is the implication $\varphi \to \bot$.

results.title: Disjunction of epistemic formulas
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The disjunction $\varphi \lor \psi$ of epistemic formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$ is the implication $\neg\varphi \to \psi$.

results.title: Satisfaction in an epistemic model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Satisfaction of an epistemic formula at a world $w$ of a model $M$ is defined by recursion on the formula, writing $R_i$ for the accessibility relation of agent $i$ in $M$ and $K_i \varphi$ for the formula "agent $i$ knows $\varphi$": an atom $a$ holds at $w$ when the valuation of $M$ makes $a$ true at $w$; $\bot$ holds at no world; $\varphi \to \psi$ holds at $w$ when $\psi$ holds at $w$ whenever $\varphi$ does;…

results.title: Validity in an epistemic model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A formula $\varphi$ is valid in an epistemic model $M$ when $\varphi$ is satisfied at every world of $M$.

results.title: Falsity is not valid in an epistemic model
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In every epistemic model, the formula $\bot$ is not valid: it fails at some world.

results.title: Satisfaction of a disjunction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In an epistemic model $M$, the disjunction $\varphi \lor \psi$ of two formulas, defined as $\neg \varphi \to \psi$, is satisfied at a world $w$ if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfied at $w$ or $\psi$ is satisfied at $w$.

results.title: Distribution axiom K
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Write $K_i \varphi$ for "agent $i$ knows $\varphi$". For every epistemic model $M$, every agent $i$ and all formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the formula $K_i (\varphi \to \psi) \to (K_i \varphi \to K_i \psi)$ is valid in $M$: knowledge distributes over implication.

results.title: Truth axiom T
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Write $K_i \varphi$ for "agent $i$ knows $\varphi$". Let $M$ be an epistemic model in which the accessibility relation $R_i$ of agent $i$ is reflexive. Then for every formula $\varphi$, the formula $K_i \varphi \to \varphi$ is valid in $M$.

results.title: Positive introspection axiom 4
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Write $K_i \varphi$ for "agent $i$ knows $\varphi$". Let $M$ be an epistemic model in which the accessibility relation $R_i$ of agent $i$ is transitive. Then for every formula $\varphi$, the formula $K_i \varphi \to K_i K_i \varphi$ is valid in $M$.

results.title: Negative introspection axiom 5
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Write $K_i \varphi$ for "agent $i$ knows $\varphi$". Let $M$ be an epistemic model in which the accessibility relation $R_i$ of agent $i$ is euclidean: for all worlds $a$, $b$, $c$, if $a \mathrel{R_i} b$ and $a \mathrel{R_i} c$ then $b \mathrel{R_i} c$. Then for every formula $\varphi$, the formula $\neg K_i \varphi \to K_i \neg K_i \varphi$ is valid in $M$.

results.title: The two-agent coin model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The epistemic model whose worlds are the two booleans, with $\mathrm{true}$ read as heads and $\mathrm{false}$ as tails, with a single atom $p$ true exactly at the heads world, and with two agents $0$ and $1$: agent $0$ sees the coin, so its accessibility relation is equality of worlds, and agent $1$ does not, so its accessibility relation relates every pair of worlds.

results.title: Agent 0 knows the coin is heads exactly at heads
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be the atom "the coin is heads" of the two-agent coin model. At a world $v$ of that model, the formula $K_0 p$ holds if and only if $v$ is the heads world: agent $0$ sees the coin.

results.title: Agent 0 knows the coin is tails exactly at tails
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be the atom "the coin is heads" of the two-agent coin model. At a world $v$ of that model, the formula $K_0 \neg p$ holds if and only if $v$ is the tails world.

results.title: Agent 1 does not know that the coin is heads
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be the atom "the coin is heads" of the two-agent coin model. The formula $K_1 p$ is false at the heads world: agent $1$ considers the tails world possible.

results.title: Agent 1 knows that agent 0 knows whether the coin is heads
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be the atom "the coin is heads" of the two-agent coin model. At every world of that model the formula $K_1(K_0 p \lor K_0 \neg p)$ holds: agent $1$ knows that agent $0$ either knows $p$ or knows $\neg p$.

results.title: PDL model
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A model of propositional dynamic logic with set of worlds $W$ consists of a binary accessibility relation $R_a$ on $W$ for each atomic action label $a$, and a valuation that says which atoms are true at each world.

results.title: PDL formulas
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: The formulas of propositional dynamic logic over a type of atoms and a type of atomic action labels are the atoms $p$, falsity $\bot$, implications $\varphi \to \psi$ of formulas, and boxes $[\alpha]\varphi$ of a program $\alpha$ and a formula $\varphi$. Formulas and programs are defined by simultaneous induction.

results.title: PDL programs
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: The programs of propositional dynamic logic over a type of atoms and a type of atomic action labels are the atomic actions $a$, sequential compositions $\alpha ; \beta$, nondeterministic choices $\alpha \cup \beta$, iterations $\alpha^*$, and tests $\varphi?$ of a formula $\varphi$. Programs and formulas are defined by simultaneous induction.

results.title: Possibility in PDL
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a program $\alpha$ and a formula $\varphi$, the formula $\langle\alpha\rangle\varphi$ is defined as $\alpha \to \bot$, that is, as $\neg[\alpha]\neg\varphi$: possibility is the dual of necessity.

results.title: Relation denoted by a PDL program
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: In a model $M$, each program $\alpha$ denotes a binary relation $R_\alpha$ on worlds: an atomic action $a$ denotes its accessibility relation $R_a$; $(w, v) \in R_{\alpha;\beta}$ iff $(w, u) \in R_\alpha$ and $(u, v) \in R_\beta$ for some world $u$; $R_{\alpha \cup \beta} = R_\alpha \cup R_\beta$; $R_{\alpha^*}$ is the reflexive-transitive closure of $R_\alpha$; and $(w, v) \in R_{\varphi?}$ iff $w = v$ and…

results.title: Satisfaction of PDL formulas
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Truth of a formula at a world $w$ of a model $M$ is defined by recursion: an atom $p$ holds at $w$ iff the valuation of $M$ makes $p$ true at $w$; $\bot$ holds nowhere; $\varphi \to \psi$ holds at $w$ iff $\psi$ holds at $w$ whenever $\varphi$ does; and $[\alpha]\varphi$ holds at $w$ iff $\varphi$ holds at every world $v$ with $(w, v) \in R_\alpha$, where $R_\alpha$ is the relation denoted by $\alpha$ in $M$.

results.title: Box of a sequential composition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every model $M$, world $w$, programs $\alpha$ and $\beta$, and formula $\varphi$, the formula $[\alpha;\beta]\varphi$ holds at $w$ if and only if $[\alpha][\beta]\varphi$ holds at $w$.

results.title: Box of a choice
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every model $M$, world $w$, programs $\alpha$ and $\beta$, and formula $\varphi$, the formula $[\alpha \cup \beta]\varphi$ holds at $w$ if and only if both $[\alpha]\varphi$ and $[\beta]\varphi$ hold at $w$.

results.title: Unfolding the box of an iteration
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every model $M$, world $w$, program $\alpha$ and formula $\varphi$, the formula $[\alpha^*]\varphi$ holds at $w$ if and only if $\varphi$ holds at $w$ and $[\alpha][\alpha^*]\varphi$ holds at $w$.

results.title: Box of a test
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every model $M$, world $w$ and formulas $\psi$ and $\varphi$, the formula $[\psi?]\varphi$ holds at $w$ if and only if $\varphi$ holds at $w$ whenever $\psi$ holds at $w$.

results.title: The toggle model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The PDL model whose worlds are the two Booleans $\mathsf{true}$ and $\mathsf{false}$, with a single atomic action $a$ and a single atom $p$: the action $a$ relates each world $s$ exactly to its negation $\lnot s$, and $p$ holds exactly at $\mathsf{true}$.

results.title: Failure of $(a;a)\,p$ in the toggle model
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In the toggle model, with atomic action $a$ and atom $p$, the formula $[a;a]\,p$ is not satisfied at the world $\mathsf{false}$.

results.title: $\kappa$-almost disjoint family of sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A family F ⊆ 𝒫(I) is *κ-almost disjoint* if |A| = κ for every A ∈ F and |A ∩ B| < κ for all distinct A, B ∈ F.

results.title: Functions almost disjoint modulo the nonstationary ideal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Functions f, g ∈ ∏_{α<ω₁} A_α are *almost disjoint mod the nonstationary ideal* if the set { α < ω₁ : f(α) = g(α) } on which they agree is nonstationary in ω₁.

results.title: Almost disjoint family of functions on a regular cardinal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let κ be a regular cardinal. A family of functions κ → κ is *almost disjoint* if for all f and g in the family with f≠ g, |{ α ∣ f(α ) = g(α ) }|<κ..

results.title: Intertwining passes to the exponential
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `A * X = X * B` for a rectangular matrix `X`, then `exp A * X = X * exp B`.

results.title: Determinant of the matrix exponential
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every complex square matrix $A$ indexed by a finite set, $\det(e^A) = e^{\operatorname{tr} A}$, where $e^A$ is the matrix exponential. This identity is sometimes called Jacobi's formula.

results.title: Exponential of a nilpotent matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $A$ is a nilpotent complex square matrix indexed by a finite set, then there is a natural number $m$ such that $e^A = \sum_{k=0}^{m-1} \frac{1}{k!} A^k$, where $e^A$ is the matrix exponential.

results.title: Cassels' embedding theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero and $S$ a finite subset of $K$. Then there are a prime $p \ge 3$ and an injective ring homomorphism from the subring of $K$ generated by $S$ into the ring $\mathbb{Z}_p$ of $p$-adic integers.

results.title: p-adic integrality is equivalent to norm at most one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An element of the algebraic closure of `ℚ_[p]` is integral over `ℤ_[p]` if and only if its norm is at most one.

results.title: Strassmann's theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $(b_m)_{m \ge 0}$ be a sequence in $\mathbb{Q}_p$, not identically zero, with $b_m \to 0$. Then the power series $\sum_{m \ge 0} b_m y^m$ has only finitely many zeros $y \in \mathbb{Q}_p$ with $|y|_p \le 1$.

results.title: Cofactor lower bound
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $m$, $m$ is a cofactor lower bound for $n$ when, for every set $A$ of exactly $n$ positive integers, the set $\{a/\gcd(a,b) : a, b \in A\}$ has at least $m$ elements.

results.title: Erdős cofactor threshold
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the cofactor threshold $h(n)$ is the largest natural number $m$ such that for every set $A$ of exactly $n$ positive integers, the set $\{a/\gcd(a,b) : a, b \in A\}$ has at least $m$ elements.

results.title: Statement of Erdős Problem 539
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $h(n)$ denote the cofactor threshold of $n$. The statement is that $\sqrt{n} = O(h(n))$ as $n \to \infty$, that is, there are a real constant $C$ and an $n_0$ such that $\sqrt{n} \le C\,h(n)$ for all natural numbers $n \ge n_0$.

results.title: Erdős Problem 539: square-root lower bound for the cofactor threshold
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $h(n)$ be the largest natural number $m$ such that for every set $A$ of exactly $n$ positive integers, the set $\{a/\gcd(a,b) : a, b \in A\}$ has at least $m$ elements. Then $\sqrt{n} = O(h(n))$ as $n \to \infty$: there are a real constant $C$ and an $n_0$ such that $\sqrt{n} \le C\,h(n)$ for all natural numbers $n \ge n_0$.

results.title: The dot product with a fixed vector
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite type $\iota$ and a vector $x \in \mathbb{R}^\iota$, this is the map $v \mapsto v \cdot x = \sum_{i \in \iota} v_i x_i$, as a continuous linear functional $\mathbb{R}^\iota \to \mathbb{R}$.

results.title: A Fréchet derivative given by a dot product is a gradient
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\iota$ be a finite type, let $f : \mathbb{R}^\iota \to \mathbb{R}$ and $g, z \in \mathbb{R}^\iota$, and suppose that, for the sup norm on $\mathbb{R}^\iota$, $f$ is Fréchet differentiable at $z$ with derivative $v \mapsto v \cdot g$. Then $f$, viewed as a function on the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^\iota$ with inner product $\langle v, w \rangle = \sum_{i \in \iota} v_i w_i$, has gradient $g$ at $z$.

results.title: Directional derivative from the gradient
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\iota$ be a finite type, let $f : \mathbb{R}^\iota \to \mathbb{R}$ and $g, z \in \mathbb{R}^\iota$, and suppose $f$ is Fréchet differentiable at $z$ with derivative $w \mapsto w \cdot g$. Then for every $v \in \mathbb{R}^\iota$, the function $t \mapsto f(z + t v)$ on $\mathbb{R}$ has derivative $v \cdot g$ at $t = 0$.

results.title: The chain rule for gradients
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ and $F$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $g : E \to F$ be differentiable at $x \in E$, and let $f : F \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at $g(x)$. Then $\nabla (f \circ g)(x) = Dg(x)^* \, \nabla f(g(x))$, where $Dg(x) : E \to F$ is the Fréchet derivative of $g$ at $x$ and $Dg(x)^*$ is its adjoint.

results.title: Erdős Problem 907
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that every function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $x \mapsto f(x + h) - f(x)$ is continuous for every $h > 0$ can be written as $f = g + a$ with $g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ continuous and $a : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ additive, that is, $a(x + y) = a(x) + a(y)$ for all real $x$ and $y$.

results.title: De Bruijn's theorem on continuous differences (Erdős Problem 907)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function such that for every $h > 0$ the function $x \mapsto f(x + h) - f(x)$ is continuous. Then there are functions $g, a : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $g$ continuous and $a$ additive, that is, $a(x + y) = a(x) + a(y)$ for all real $x$ and $y$, such that $f = g + a$.

results.title: Grouped right-censored survival data
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Right-censored survival data grouped at `k` distinct, increasing observation times: `deaths j` subjects die and `censored j` subjects are censored at `time j`.

results.title: Sample size of censored survival data
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The number of subjects in the sample.

results.title: Number at risk at an observation time
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The number at risk at `time j`: subjects whose observation time is at least `time j`.

results.title: Kaplan–Meier factor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Kaplan–Meier factor `1 - dⱼ / nⱼ` at `time j` (it is `1` if nobody is at risk, where also `dⱼ = 0`).

results.title: Kaplan–Meier survival estimate
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Kaplan–Meier estimate `Ŝ(t) = ∏_{tⱼ ≤ t} (1 - dⱼ / nⱼ)` of the survival function.

results.title: Kaplan–Meier jump at an observation time
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Kaplan–Meier jump at `time j`: `Ŝ(tⱼ₋) · dⱼ / nⱼ`.

results.title: Kaplan–Meier mass after the last observation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Kaplan–Meier mass left after the last observation time, `∏ⱼ (1 - dⱼ / nⱼ)`.

results.title: Kaplan–Meier measure
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Kaplan–Meier measure: the jumps `kmMass j` at `time j` and the leftover mass `kmTail` at a chosen point `τ` (taken after the last observation time).

results.title: Likelihood of right-censored data
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The censored-data likelihood of a law `μ` of the survival time: `∏ⱼ μ{tⱼ}^{dⱼ} · μ(tⱼ, ∞)^{cⱼ}`.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The deaths at a time are among those at risk.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Kaplan–Meier factor is at most `1`.

results.title: Kaplan–Meier factor is nonnegative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Kaplan–Meier factor is non-negative.

results.title: Kaplan–Meier jumps are nonnegative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Kaplan–Meier jumps are non-negative.

results.title: Leftover Kaplan–Meier mass is nonnegative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The leftover Kaplan–Meier mass is non-negative.

results.title: Kaplan–Meier jumps and leftover mass sum to one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Kaplan–Meier jumps and the leftover mass add up to `1`.

results.title: Mass of a set under the Kaplan–Meier measure

results.title: Kaplan–Meier measure is a probability measure
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Kaplan–Meier measure is a probability measure.

results.title: Survival function of the Kaplan–Meier measure
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The survival function of the Kaplan–Meier measure is the Kaplan–Meier estimate on `(-∞, τ)`: `P(T > t) = Ŝ(t)` for `t < τ`.

results.title: Kaplan–Meier is the nonparametric MLE
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Kaplan–Meier is the nonparametric MLE (Kaplan–Meier 1958): every probability measure on `ℝ` has censored-data likelihood at most that of the Kaplan–Meier measure.

results.title: Kaplan–Meier survival is positive at a censoring time
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A time at which some subject is censored has positive Kaplan–Meier survival.

results.title: Self-consistency
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Self-consistency (Efron 1967, (7.4)): `n Ŝ(t)` is the number of observations exceeding `t` plus, for each subject censored at or before `t`, the conditional survival `Ŝ(t) / Ŝ(tⱼ)`.

results.title: Kaplan–Meier estimate without censoring is the empirical survival
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Without censoring, the Kaplan–Meier estimate is the empirical survival function: the fraction `#{observations > t} / n = 1 - Fₙ(t)`.

results.title: Size of the larger of the sumset and the product set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $A$ of real numbers, this is the natural number $\max(|A+A|, |AA|)$, where $A+A = \{a+b : a, b \in A\}$ is the sumset and $AA = \{ab : a, b \in A\}$ is the product set of $A$.

results.title: Sum-product ratio
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $A$ of real numbers, the sum-product ratio of $A$ is $\log \max(|A+A|, |AA|) / \log |A|$, where $A+A$ and $AA$ are the sumset and the product set of $A$. With the conventions $\log 0 = 0$ and $x / 0 = 0$, the ratio is $0$ when $|A| \le 1$.

results.title: Sum-product ratios at a fixed cardinality
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $A \subset \mathbb{R}$ write $A + A$ and $AA$ for the sets of all sums $a + b$ and all products $ab$ with $a, b \in A$. For a natural number $n \ge 2$, this is the set of the real numbers $\log \max(|A + A|, |AA|) / \log |A|$ for all sets $A \subset \mathbb{R}$ with $|A| = n$; for $n \le 1$ it consists of the single number $0$.

results.title: Least sum-product ratio at a fixed cardinality
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the level minimum $m(n)$ is the infimum of the sum-product ratios $\log \max(|A+A|, |AA|) / \log |A|$ over all sets $A$ of $n$ real numbers, where $A+A$ and $AA$ are the sumset and the product set of $A$, and the ratio is taken to be $0$ when $|A| \le 1$ (conventions $\log 0 = 0$ and $x / 0 = 0$).

results.title: The level minimum is attained
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, let $m(n)$ be the infimum of the sum-product ratios $\log \max(|A+A|, |AA|) / \log |A|$ over all sets $A$ of $n$ real numbers, where $A+A$ and $AA$ are the sumset and the product set of $A$ and the ratio is taken to be $0$ when $|A| \le 1$ (conventions $\log 0 = 0$ and $x / 0 = 0$). Then $m(n)$ is the least element of the set of these ratios: it is the ratio of some set of $n$ real…

results.title: The sum-product ratio is nonnegative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every nonempty finite set $A$ of real numbers, the sum-product ratio $\log \max(|A+A|, |AA|) / \log |A|$ is at least $0$, where $A+A$ and $AA$ are the sumset and the product set of $A$, and the ratio is taken to be $0$ when $|A| = 1$ (conventions $\log 0 = 0$ and $x / 0 = 0$).

results.title: The sum-product ratio is at most two
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite set $A$ of real numbers with $|A| \ge 2$, the sum-product ratio $\log \max(|A+A|, |AA|) / \log |A|$ is at most $2$, where $A+A$ and $AA$ are the sumset and the product set of $A$.

results.title: The level minimum is nonnegative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 1$, the level minimum $m(n)$, the infimum of the sum-product ratios $\log \max(|A+A|, |AA|) / \log |A|$ over all sets $A$ of $n$ real numbers, satisfies $m(n) \ge 0$. Here $A+A$ and $AA$ are the sumset and the product set of $A$, and the ratio is taken to be $0$ when $|A| = 1$ (conventions $\log 0 = 0$, $x / 0 = 0$).

results.title: The level minimum is at most two
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 2$, the level minimum $m(n)$, the infimum of the sum-product ratios $\log \max(|A+A|, |AA|) / \log |A|$ over all sets $A$ of $n$ real numbers, where $A+A$ and $AA$ are the sumset and the product set of $A$, satisfies $m(n) \le 2$.

results.title: The sum-product level minima eventually lie in $(0, 2)$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a finite set $A \subset \mathbb{R}$ write $A + A$ and $AA$ for the sets of all sums $a + b$ and all products $ab$ with $a, b \in A$. For a natural number $n \ge 2$ let $m_n$ be the least value of $\log \max(|A + A|, |AA|) / \log n$ over sets $A \subset \mathbb{R}$ with $|A| = n$. Then $0 \le m_n \le 2$ for every sufficiently large $n$.

results.title: The level minima are eventually bounded above
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a real number $b$ such that $m(n) \le b$ for all sufficiently large natural numbers $n$, where the level minimum $m(n)$ is the infimum of the sum-product ratios $\log \max(|A+A|, |AA|) / \log |A|$ over all sets $A$ of $n$ real numbers, and $A+A$ and $AA$ are the sumset and the product set of $A$.

results.title: The sum-product level minima are eventually bounded below
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a real number $b$ such that the sum-product level minimum $m(n)$ satisfies $m(n) \ge b$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

results.title: Sum-product exponent of the reals
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $m(n)$ be the sum-product level minimum: the least value of $\log \max(|A + A|, |AA|) / \log |A|$ over sets $A \subset \mathbb{R}$ with $n$ elements, where $A + A$ and $AA$ are the sets of sums $a + b$ and products $ab$ of elements $a, b \in A$. The real sum-product exponent is $\liminf_{n \to \infty} m(n)$.

results.title: The sum-product exponent ignores sets of size $0$ and $1$

results.title: Value of a permutation at a natural position
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a permutation $\tau$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, d - 1\}$ and a natural number $j$, this is the natural number $\tau(j)$ when $j < d$, and $0$ when $j \ge d$. It is used to read off descents.

results.title: Descent set of a permutation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a permutation $\tau$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, d - 1\}$, the descent set is $\mathrm{Des}(\tau) = \{p \in \{1, \dots, d - 1\} : \tau(p - 1) > \tau(p)\}$. If $\tau$ is read as the permutation $p \mapsto \tau(p - 1) + 1$ of $\{1, \dots, d\}$, this is the usual descent set: the positions $p$, numbered from $1$, where the value at $p$ exceeds the value at $p + 1$.

results.title: Number of descents from the descent set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a permutation $\tau$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, d - 1\}$, the number of descents $\mathrm{des}(\tau) = |\mathrm{Des}(\tau)|$ is the number of elements of the descent set $\mathrm{Des}(\tau)$.

results.title: Major index of a permutation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a permutation $\tau$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, d - 1\}$, the major index is $\mathrm{maj}(\tau) = \sum_{p \in \mathrm{Des}(\tau)} p$, the sum of the positions, numbered from $1$, in the descent set $\mathrm{Des}(\tau)$.

results.title: Euler–Mahonian polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $d$ and elements $x, y$ of a commutative ring, the Euler–Mahonian polynomial evaluated at $(x, y)$ is $E_d(x, y) = \sum_{\tau \in S_d} x^{\operatorname{des}(\tau)} y^{\operatorname{maj}(\tau)}$, where $\operatorname{des}(\tau)$ is the number of descents and $\operatorname{maj}(\tau)$ the major index of the permutation $\tau$.

results.title: The first Euler–Mahonian polynomial is $1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every commutative ring $R$ and all $x, y \in R$, the Euler–Mahonian polynomial $E_1$ satisfies $E_1(x, y) = 1$.

results.title: Euler–Mahonian polynomial $E_3$ at $(2, 3)$

results.title: Permutations of $S_3$ with descent set $\{1\}$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Exactly two permutations $\tau \in S_3$ have exactly one descent and major index $1$, that is, $\operatorname{des}(\tau) = 1$ and $\operatorname{maj}(\tau) = 1$; equivalently, their descent set is $\{1\}$.

results.title: The partition function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, $p(n)$ is the number of partitions of $n$, that is, of ways of writing $n$ as a sum of positive integers, disregarding order.

results.title: The partition number of zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$. Then $p(0) = 1$: the only partition of $0$ is the empty one.

results.title: The partition number of one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$. Then $p(1) = 1$: the only partition of $1$ is $1$ itself.

results.title: Partition generating function with unit weights
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$. Over the integers, $\sum_{n \ge 0} p(n)\, x^n$ equals the weighted partition generating function $\sum_{n \ge 0} \sum_{\lambda} \prod_{i} f(i, c_i(\lambda))\, x^n$ with all weights $f(i, c) = 1$, where $\lambda$ runs over the partitions of $n$, $i$ over the distinct parts of $\lambda$, and $c_i(\lambda)$ is the number of times $i$ occurs in $\lambda$.

results.title: Euler's identity for the partition generating function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$. Over the integers, $\left(\sum_{n \ge 0} p(n)\, x^n\right) \cdot \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} (-1)^k x^{k(3k-1)/2} = 1$. By the pentagonal number theorem the second factor equals $\prod_{i \ge 1} (1 - x^i)$.

results.title: Euler's pentagonal recurrence for the partition function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$, and for an integer $k$ let $g(k) = k(3k - 1)/2$ be the generalized pentagonal number of $k$. For every natural number $n \ge 1$, $p(n) = \sum_{k} (-1)^{k+1}\, p(n - g(k))$, where the sum runs over the nonzero integers $k$ with $g(k) \le n$.

results.caption: Definition

results.title: A predicate recognizable by a multi-tape machine is recursively enumerable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a primcodable type (it has an encoding $\mathrm{encode} : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ whose decoding is primitive recursive). If a predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ is recognizable by a multi-tape machine, then $p$ is recursively enumerable, that is, the partial function on $\alpha$ that is defined, with a trivial value, exactly where $p$ holds is partial recursive.

results.title: A predicate decided by a multi-tape machine is recursively enumerable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a primcodable type (it has an encoding $\mathrm{encode} : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ whose decoding is primitive recursive). results.title: A predicate decided by a multi-tape machine has a recursively enumerable complement
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: A predicate decided by a multi-tape machine is computable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a primcodable type (it has an encoding $\mathrm{encode} : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ whose decoding is primitive recursive). If a predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ is decidable by a multi-tape machine, then $p$ is computable, that is, $p$ is decidable and its Boolean characteristic function $\alpha \to \mathrm{Bool}$ is computable.

results.title: Multi-tape machines decide no more than multi-stack machines

results.title: Two-locus diploid genotype under random union of gametes
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A diploid two-locus genotype under random union of gametes: the haplotypes `(X₁, Y₁)` and `(X₂, Y₂)` are independent and identically distributed, with square-integrable allele codings.

results.title: Allele frequency at the first locus
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The allele frequency (mean coding) `p = E X₁` at locus `A`.

results.title: Allele frequency at the second locus
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The allele frequency (mean coding) `q = E Y₁` at locus `B`.

results.title: Haplotype variance at the first locus
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The haplotype variance `V_A = E (X₁ - p)²` at locus `A`.

results.title: Haplotype variance at the second locus
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The haplotype variance `V_B = E (Y₁ - q)²` at locus `B`.

results.title: Gametic linkage disequilibrium
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The gametic linkage disequilibrium `D = E (X₁ - p) (Y₁ - q)`.

results.title: Additive coding at the first locus
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The additive coding `a_A = (X₁ - p) + (X₂ - p)` (centred allele count) at locus `A`.

results.title: Additive coding at the second locus
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The additive coding `a_B = (Y₁ - q) + (Y₂ - q)` at locus `B`.

results.title: Dominance coding at the first locus
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The dominance coding `d_A = (X₁ - p) (X₂ - p)` at locus `A`.

results.title: Dominance coding at the second locus
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The dominance coding `d_B = (Y₁ - q) (Y₂ - q)` at locus `B`.

results.title: Additive linkage disequilibrium is twice the gametic one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Additive LD: `E(a_A a_B) = 2 D`.

results.title: Second moment of the additive coding at the first locus
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The additive coding has second moment `E(a_A²) = 2 V_A`.

results.title: Second moment of the additive coding at the second locus
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The additive coding has second moment `E(a_B²) = 2 V_B`.

results.title: Dominance linkage disequilibrium is the square of the gametic one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Dominance LD: `E(d_A d_B) = D²`.

results.title: Second moment of the dominance coding at the first locus
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The dominance coding has second moment `E(d_A²) = V_A²`.

results.title: Second moment of the dominance coding at the second locus
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The dominance coding has second moment `E(d_B²) = V_B²`.

results.title: Additive and dominance codings at different loci are uncorrelated
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The additive coding at `A` and the dominance coding at `B` are uncorrelated: `E(a_A d_B) = 0`.

results.title: Correlation of additive codings equals the gametic correlation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The correlation of the additive codings is the gametic correlation `r = D / √(V_A V_B)`.

results.title: Dominance LD is the square of additive LD
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Dominance LD is the square of additive LD (Palmer et al. 2023, graphical abstract): the correlation of the dominance codings at two loci is the square of the correlation of their additive codings.

results.title: Dominance encoding of a biallelic genotype
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The dominance encoding of a biallelic genotype `g ∈ {0, 1, 2}` (count of the allele with frequency `p`): `p²`, `-p (1 - p)`, `(1 - p)²`. Dividing by `-p (1 - p)` gives the encoding `-p / (1 - p)`, `1`, `-(1 - p) / p` of Palmer et al. (2023).

results.title: Dominance coding of allele indicators equals the dominance encoding
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `0`/`1` allele indicators the dominance coding `(X₁ - p) (X₂ - p)` depends only on the genotype `X₁ + X₂` and equals its dominance encoding.
